edits.text: As a last resort, prefer a cut at the token that closes the preceding predicate or that identifies a noun (the verb or object token, or the noun's identifying token) over a cut at the immediately following token that begins a relative/complement clause, an essential prepositional complement, or a quoted multiword complement.

Prefer a cut after the closing token of the preceding predicate or noun phrase over cutting before an immediately following relative/complement clause, an essential prepositional complement, or a quoted multiword complement that completes or disambiguates it.

Prefer a cut after a short (≤6-word) clausal or complement continuation over a cut immediately before it when the following span begins with a complementizer/relative pronoun, essential preposition, or opening parenthesis and syntactically completes or disambiguates the preceding predicate or noun.
